lines: The week's done, every bay is empty, and every ship is flying home. They called the fighters important and the freighters tough. Nobody mentioned who kept them both going.
Big talk from the fighters, big dents from the freighters. Guess who fixed the lot of them. The quiet one with the spanners turned out to be the one they needed.
Seven days, and the station still stands. Pride is nice to polish, but I'll polish the spanners first. Same bays next run, same grin.

report.reason: The set grins and brags without being mean to the player. Line 2 is cheeky, and line 3 is proud and playful. Line 1 is a little drier but still has the dig at the ships.
Nothing sounds rich, high-tech or wasteful. Spanners and polishing them are humble, hands-on images.
Only the player speaks. 'The quiet one with the spanners' refers to the player, and no other mechanic, crew or successor appears.

Lines 1 and 2 brag that the overlooked mechanic proved who is important, which is the moment's job. Line 3 is more a humble sign-off ('I'll polish the spanners first', 'Same bays next run') and its bragging is weak. It also promises a next run, which is not part of the job.
report.evidence: Pride is nice to polish, but I'll polish the spanners first. Same bays next run, same grin.

report.reason: No swap trick, no moving parts between ships, no percentage levels.
Fighters, freighters, bays and the station are all in the game's world. Nothing is invented. 'Every ship is flying home' is a slight stretch, since ships just exit, but it is harmless.
The station is shown only through bays, spanners and polishing tools, which suit a rugged, tidy place. It is never shiny and never a mess.
